body: The bugs are drying up and my todo list is complete, so I'm marking this as ready for review! I expect this will likely require more work to finish, and it still fails certain auto-run checks due to compatibility breakages (notably with GDExtension), but I think it's stable enough to stop calling it a draft ^^

This is fantastic work! Thank you so much for this effort. If it's not too late to consider, I'd like to offer a few suggestions that would greatly expand the kinds of connections `GraphEdit` could create, making it easier to generate orthogonally connected flow chart/schematic diagrams without becoming too specialized. I have experience implementing a complete diagramming application like Visio (not in Godot). **For the new `GraphPort`:** I think an additional enum specifying the vector direction of the connection attached to the port should be added, which is a different concept than the input/output flow of information now in the `PortDirection`. Maybe rename `PortDirection` to `PortFlowDirection`. Also add to it a `BIDIRECTIONAL` member which will inform the potential use of an arrowhead at a port. There are cases where a `GraphNode` symbol could have a `GraphPort` with an ambiguous connection vector start/end direction, so custom connection line routing code should be provided that direction. I've attached a couple of examples of symbols with ambiguous port vector directions where relying on the port relationship to the `Rect2` extents of the `GraphNode` to compute the direction vector would not work. In general, any port not on the rectangular perimeter of the `GraphNode` or in a corner will have an ambiguous vector direction. ``` enum PortFlowDirection { INPUT, OUTPUT, BIDIRECTIONAL, UNDIRECTED }; enum PortConnectionDirection { NORTH, SOUTH, EAST, WEST, OMNIDIRECTIONAL }; ``` Now modify `GraphEdit::get_connection_line()` to pass the ports so a virtual method can create a line using the connection directions. ` virtual PackedVector2Array get_connection_line(const Vector2 &p_from, const Vector2 &p_to, GraphPort &p_from_port, GraphPort &p_to_port) const;` It would be nice to add a `text` property to `GraphPort` so ports can be named. This would allow automatic connection from/to labeling and `GraphNode` port naming. The port type naming scheme via a `Dictionary` in `GraphEdit` seems like an unusual pattern in Godot that must have been in response to the old automatic port indexing architecture. I wonder if it would make sense to remove that in favor of the port name being solely a property of `GraphPort`? **Connection Arrowheads** Since you now have the ports provided with the `GraphEdit::connection_request` signal, we can obtain both port's `PortFlowDirection` and `PortConnectionDirection`, which is enough to determine if an arrowhead should be added and in what orientation. It would be fantastic if you could actually implement arrowheads with this PR, but optional and could be done in a future PR. It's slightly non-intuitive to add the arrowheads to `GraphPort`, but I think that's the place to do it. First we add a theme icon for the arrowhead to `GraphPort`. I've attached an example arrowhead `SVGTexture` resource. Then in `GraphEdit` expose a `connection_arrowheads` property: ``` enum ConnectionArrowheads { ARROWHEAD_INPUT_OR_BIDIRECTIONAL, ARROWHEAD_BOTH_ENDS, ARROWHEAD_NONE }; ConnectionArrowheads connection_arrowheads = ARROWHEAD_NONE; ``` Add the property to `GraphPort`, and this property determines if the arrowhead gets added in `NOTIFICATION_DRAW`, and it's oriented in accordance with `PortConnectionDirection`: ``` GraphEdit::ConnectionArrowheads connection_arrowheads = graph_edit->connection_arrowheads; ``` **Misc** When resizing a `GraphNode`, holding down the ALT key should lock the `GraphNode` aspect ratio. I think connection colors should also be able to be set independently of their port color. `SVGTexture` arrowhead icon: [graph_port_arrowhead.tres.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/21720663/graph_port_arrowhead.tres.zip)

> an additional enum specifying the vector direction of the connection attached to the port should be added

I agree that adding control over the direction connections should enter/exit the port would be a good idea. For flexibility, I think this might be best encoded as a float angle in degrees, rather than an enum, and it would be nice to make it a theme item.

Additionally, splitting it into multiple values would allow independent control over the direction of input, output, and undirected connections on a single port, which i can see being handy. 

> Also add to it a `BIDIRECTIONAL` member

How does this differ from Undirected? For reference, an Undirected port allows connections from other ports regardless of their direction. Do you mean that this port should, when connected, assign itself an implicit direction based on that connection?

> It would be nice to add a `text` property to `GraphPort` so ports can be named.

Agreed! Though, figuring out the right layout behaviours for that text sounds like quite a task. I think this would warrant a whole followup PR. Plus, `GraphPort` being a node means it's extensible, so adding features like that can even be handled in script ^^

> The port type naming scheme via a `Dictionary` in `GraphEdit` seems like an unusual pattern in Godot that must have been in response to the old automatic port indexing architecture.

Quite unusual yeah. I believe it's being used somewhere in the visual shader editor (possibly for screen reader things?), though to be honest I don't know what it's even used for. Regardless, it's separate from naming the port, since it's naming the *type* of a port. 


> It would be fantastic if you could actually implement arrowheads with this PR, but optional and could be done in a future PR.

I'm veto-ing this for this PR, but it sounds like a good feature for a followup PR.

This also makes me think it would be a good idea to split a port's theme icon to allow icons to be assigned to input, output, and undirected ports at the theme level. 

> **Misc** When resizing a `GraphNode`, holding down the ALT key should lock the `GraphNode` aspect ratio.

Oo alright, yea good idea. 

> I think connection colors should also be able to be set independently of their port color.

Also good idea - adding a color override property for each end of the connection would be useful. 

Thanks for the suggestions!

> I agree that adding control over the direction connections should enter/exit the port would be a good idea. For flexibility, I think this might be best encoded as a float angle in degrees, rather than an enum, and it would be nice to make it a theme item.
> 
Seems to me it should be a property rather than a theme setting, because each port will have it calculated or determined individually, and there is no case where one theme setting would work for all ports.

One advantage of having the compass directions as enum choices, is you avoid having to compare floats to check if the angle is orthoganal, which would be error-prone. The compass enums could be set to ints 0, 90, 180 and 270 and cast to a float for the angle var, and the angle property could be exposed and used only when the direction is OMNIDIRECTIONAL.

Custom routing logic would use something like a lookup table given the start and end directions for all possible routings, so a `Dictionary` key would be something like `[NORTH, EAST]` so you'd want the directions as enums as a matter of convenience.
> Additionally, splitting it into multiple values would allow independent control over the direction of input, output, and undirected connections on a single port, which i can see being handy.
>
Interesting idea - might be too specialized since that could be done by the routing logic? Which brings up a thought about `GraphConnection` (for future PR with arrowheads  per your comment below) - I wondered if connections should store the direction obtained from the port, and then draw the arrowhead there? Then if you had different input/output directions the code might be simpler. Also if you delete a connection it automatically takes the arrowhead with it. So is there any other reason why we might want to store the start/end directions in `GraphConnection`?
> > Also add to it a `BIDIRECTIONAL` member
> 
> How does this differ from Undirected? For reference, an Undirected port allows connections from other ports regardless of their direction. Do you mean that this port should, when connected, assign itself an implicit direction based on that connection?
> 
Yes, I was uncertain what Undirected implied - does this mean it becomes the polar opposite of what you connect it to? If so, that's different from Bidirectional in terms of being what determines whether or not to use an arrowhead. If the intent is information flows in both directions, then maybe Bidirectional is a bit more precise?
> > It would be nice to add a `text` property to `GraphPort` so ports can be named.
> 
> Agreed! Though, figuring out the right layout behaviours for that text sounds like quite a task. I think this would warrant a whole followup PR. Plus, `GraphPort` being a node means it's extensible, so adding features like that can even be handled in script ^^
>
Here I was meaning the `text` property is just for the name of the port, and where to show that with a `Label` or something would be handled elsewhere.
> > The port type naming scheme via a `Dictionary` in `GraphEdit` seems like an unusual pattern in Godot that must have been in response to the old automatic port indexing architecture.
> 
> Quite unusual yeah. I believe it's being used somewhere in the visual shader editor (possibly for screen reader things?), though to be honest I don't know what it's even used for. Regardless, it's separate from naming the port, since it's naming the _type_ of a port.
>
Isn't the port name a string for whatever the type enum int is? I'll try to hunt down how that's used in visual shader editor, but it seems like the naming assignments would always be handled by the class implementing `GraphEdit` and would then do it by port if it had a name/text property. Maybe this PR shouldn't try to move that code up to `VisualShader`, but it would decouple things better if it were not in `GraphEdit`.

I also had a question about this PR's `type_colors` `Array` - should this be in `GraphEdit` at all per above? A parent class could manage the port type->color info. If it stays, it seems like it needs to be a `Dictionary` like `type_names` so the port type ints can be any set of values instead of only sequential.
> > It would be fantastic if you could actually implement arrowheads with this PR, but optional and could be done in a future PR.
> 
> I'm veto-ing this for this PR, but it sounds like a good feature for a followup PR.
> 
This is a good choice and can be done later, and easily if we lay the groundwork.
> This also makes me think it would be a good idea to split a port's theme icon to allow icons to be assigned to input, output, and undirected ports at the theme level.
>
Yes, and then the icon draws per the `PortFlowDirection` - although this could be added in a future PR too.

Thanks again for your work on this!

> Seems to me it should be a property rather than a theme setting, because each port will have it calculated or determined individually.

Typically from what I've seen, graphs have consistent directions of travel for better readability - inputs and outputs flow from left to right, top to bottom, etc. Obviously, I want to make this system flexible enough to support graphs that break this, but I'd prefer to make the most commonly-traveled path the one with least resistance. Hence, encode direction as a theme item to let users with consistently-directed ports "fire and forget" their port angles, but still allow users with more complex graphs override these values on a per-port basis just fine ^^

I agree that it makes orthogonality checks slightly more difficult, but most projects don't need to compare the precise angle their ports provide to connections in script. For the ones that do, something simple like `floor(port1.conn_direction) == floor(port2.conn_direction)` should do the trick.

> I wondered if connections should store the direction obtained from the port, and then draw the arrowhead there?

Yep, drawing the arrowhead using the connection makes complete sense to me! There's already logic in the drawing of the connection that accesses a port's direction for this purpose.

> Yes, I was uncertain what Undirected implied - does this mean it becomes the polar opposite of what you connect it to?

Alright, so here's how the directions work:
- A port marked as `INPUT` may make connections to an `OUTPUT` or `UNDIRECTED` port. It may not make connections to another `INPUT` port.
- A port marked as `OUTPUT` may make connections to an `INPUT` or `UNDIRECTED` port. It may not make connections to another `OUTPUT` port.
- A port marked as `UNDIRECTED` may make connections to any port, regardless of direction. An `UNDIRECTED` port may be connected to both `INPUT` and `OUTPUT` ports (even at the same time!). Think of it as a "this port ignores directions" option - it is non-directed.

There's room here to add some behaviour that, like you assumed with `BIDIRECTIONAL`, makes a port undirected by default, but imply its direction from its first connection to another directed port (if it has a connection). I haven't run into this yet, as an `UNDIRECTED` port that allows more than one connection (IE is not `exclusive`) is something of a niche use case, but it'd certainly be useful in that case.

> Here I was meaning the text property is just for the name of the port, and where to show that with a Label or something would be handled elsewhere.

True, but I think both the property and the behaviour that displays it with a `Label` should be added at the same time, as adding an unused property to the engine is kinda bad practice.

The hard part of that whole task would be designing the layout behaviour for that label - lots of tricky design decisions in making it flexible for custom text layouts but still friendly to use with little-to-no input for the majority of projects. If someone wants to test that out, an intermediate step some folks take is writing a GDExtension to experiment with things - I think it might be a good approach.

> I also had a question about this PR's type_colors Array - should this be in GraphEdit at all per above?

If it's stored in either the `GraphNode` or `GraphPort`, it has to be serialized in _every_ `GraphNode`/`GraphPort`, so this saves a great deal on storage. But, more importantly, I found it was pretty terrible practice for port types and type colors to be determined locally within the same graph. If two ports in the same graph have the same port type number, they should _be_ the same type semantically as well - type `1` shouldn't be, say, `int` in one place and `Oregano` in another. Similarly, if two ports have the same icon and color, it indicates they're the same type. There's exceptions, like if `1` is `int` and `12` is `enum`, it's fine to make them both the same shade of cyan (so long as you call `GraphEdit.add_valid_connection_type` to make them interchangeable to the user). But from a UX point of view, the user should be presented with a consistent, uniform color palette that signals "light blue can be connected to light blue", and making the port type color palette local to either `GraphNode` or `GraphPort` is just asking for projects to break this pattern for very little gain. I find making this a graph-global property discourages bad port-typing practice across the board.

This logic probably also applies to type names, but for this PR, I'm likely not going to touch that property lol.

Anyway, you're definitely right, it should be a typed dictionary instead of an array :P

Ty for the feedback!

@Koyper based on your suggestions, I've done the following:
- Added `GraphPort.imply_direction`, which will make a port decide its direction based on the first connection to an input or output port
- Changed `GraphEdit.type_colors` to a `Dictionary[int, Color]`
- Added `GraphPort.get_connection_angle`, which is driven by some theme items and used to control connection line angles.

> @Koyper based on your suggestions, I've done the following:
> 

Great! I'm going to experiment with this and will give comments later. In the meantime, have you thought about the idea of having an `HGraphPort` and `VGraphPort` extending `GraphPort` like we do with `SplitContainer` and `BoxContainer`? This might simplify using the hotzone theme settings, etc. and any future `Label` settings.

Regarding a port `Label`: I think you could get away with just three label properties - `label_quadrant` - UL, UR, LL, LR (these set the label H&V text alignments), `label_v_offset`, and `label_h_offset`, and assume the label will always be horizontal.

You will also need to squash your commits at some point.

> You will also need to squash your commits at some point.

This is not an issue until it's fully reviewed and ready to merge, until then it's up to you what works best for your workflow

> have you thought about the idea of having an `HGraphPort` and `VGraphPort`?

The H and V hotzone constants refer to width and height, not horizontal and vertical port orientation. Ports will still need width and height settings in either orientation, so that change would not simplify those properties.

In any case, I think it would probably be best to stick to the base `GraphPort` class in-engine. Ports are usually more-or-less square, and shouldn't be used as layout containers like `HBoxContainer`.

Separately, I _do_ see a use case for a `VGraphNodeIndexed`/`HGraphNodeIndexed` split. That's worth considering for another PR ^^

Some initial comments, starting with curiosity about why historically `GraphEdit` was setup for pan and zoom using scale and position changing for each `GraphElement` instead of as a `Viewport` with a `Camera2D`? Is this actually _more_ performant for large graphs? Fairly complicated rigging in there with the `ViewPanner`. I'm definitely not suggesting changing this. This came up while I was hunting down why child `Controls` of `GraphEdit` don't zoom and pan.

Is it too early to report issues with `VisualShader`?

I think `GraphElements` without `GraphPorts` should still draw in the minimap. Currently they are invisible in the minimap even when they contain labels or other visible controls. In `_minimap_draw()` there is duplicate code with two `for` loops. One each for `GraphFrame` and `GraphNode`. These could be combined into one with a `switch` and include `GraphElement` so those are also drawn.

I really like the new `imply_direction` property, but it would be most useful if an imply direction port were also automatically set to `Output` if it's the first port selected when dragging in a connector. This way you could have graph elements where all the ports were imply, that could be freely connected up in any combination of directions simply by the order in which you pick the starting ports. This would be super useful for many kinds of diagrams. I'm still thinking about the case of actual bidirectional ports, one example being a bus of some kind.

I'd like to propose a new `GraphEdit` method `get_tool_menu_control()` that returns the tool internal `Control` node, so you can move or reparent it or add additional items to it. Document that the first child is an `HBoxContainer` that contains all the tool items,  and provide the standard don't free the internal node warning.

> Why doesn't `GraphEdit` use a `Viewport` with a `Camera2D`? 

No idea tbh! It seems like a redundant solution to a solved problem, but there could be reasons.

> Is it too early to report issues with `VisualShader`?

Nope, please fire away, I want to squash regressions there asap.

> I think GraphElements without GraphPorts should still draw in the minimap. 

Agreed! Plus, I was thinking about making `GraphPort`s with no parent be drawn in the minimap, so drawing all `GraphElement`s would also accomplish that. 

> It would be most useful if an imply direction port were also automatically set to `Output` if it's the first port selected when dragging in a connector. 

That's an excellent idea! Yeah, If both ports in a connection are implied, I think it makes sense to infer that from user input.

> I'd like to propose a new `GraphEdit` method `get_tool_menu_control()` that returns the tool internal `Control` node, so you can move or reparent it or add additional items to it.

~~Also a good idea! Consider it done.~~ Hey wait, isn't this just `GraphEdit.get_menu_hbox`?

> Hey wait, isn't this just `GraphEdit.get_menu_hbox`?

Doy! I was looking for a `Control` return method. Proposal resolved!

Wow, things are shaping up. Well done!

I've hardly touched `VisualShader` yet so not much to report, but the editor crashes when changing Vector Compose `Vector3` to `Vector4` or `Vector2`.

Really nice that you can have standalone `GraphPorts`!

I know these suggestions involve a lot of work for you, so just pick and choose what you think makes sense.

Just something to think about: these rename suggestions are asking a lot so probably not an option, but this is a super rare opportunity to do it, and I think it makes the names more consistent with other container types.

- Rename `GraphElement` to `GraphElementContainer` and change the icon to resemble the current `GraphFrame` icon, which fits in with other `Container` type icons. It seems like `GraphElementContainer` could inherit `PanelContainer` - I can't immediately think of a reason why not? 
- Change the `GraphFrame` icon to look more like a square box with three or four dots or pixels inside it.
- Rename `GraphNode` to `GraphPortContainer`
- Rename `GraphNodeIndexed` to `GraphPortContainerIndexed`
- Right now `GraphPortContainer` and `GraphPortContainerIndexed` share the same icon - I suggest changing the `GraphPortContainer` icon so that the two port dots are unfilled just like the port shown in the current `GraphFrame` icon, and possibly putting one of the two dots on the bottom of the icon instead of on the side.

Fantastic to be able to set the minimap panel! I think there should be a new theme constant setting `use_panel_for_minimap` defaulting to disabled, that causes the minimap panel to use the theme panel stylebox. If `GraphElement` (`GraphElementContainer`) inherited `PanelContainer` instead of `Container`, you could then add the constant to `GraphElementContainer`.

`GraphFrame` autoshrink - I don't think this actually works as described in the docs. For example, it still sorts children like a container when autoshrink is disabled - shouldn't it act like a `Control` when disabled? Probably issues in here that you know about already.

On drag, snap `position + pivot_offset` to the grid, not just `position`. This allows positioning nodes with their centerlines in alignment, which is expected behavior with many diagrams. Since the `pivot_offset` is by default `Vector2(0, 0)`the default behavior will be the same as it is now. It would be cool if during drag, a red (for example) vertical, and green horizonal line were drawn through the pivot point, so you can see how you are aligned to distant nodes.

There is a bug that the above would fix: if you zoom and a `GraphElement` has a `pivot_offset`, the node slides against the grid because zoom is not accounting for `pivot_offset`.

Also, resizing a graph node should resize around the `pivot_offset`, not `position`. This will behave as now unless the `pivot_offset` is not `Vector2(0, 0)`, in which case it would then hold its snapped grid position when resized.

If you were to specifically exclude the `top_layer` `Control` (and all other stationary internal `Controls`) from zoom/pan and minimap, is there any reason why all other `Control` children of `GraphEdit` shouldn't act like they are inside a `GraphElement`? It seems like an artificial limitation not to be able to simply add any `Control` child to `GraphEdit` and have it appear as part of the graph, but `GraphEdit` ignores otherwise.

It would be super useful to be able to disable `GraphEdit` so that nothing is editable and zoom/pan are locked. While you can go through and disable all the children, it seems like there's no way to disable pan and zoom?

Hi @Koyper, great feedback, but I don't concur with the rename of `GraphNode`.

With respect, I understand your intent here with aligning with other GUI elements, but at the same time, I do wonder if eliminating the idea of "node" in the class name could be more confusing for users. In visual graphs, it's commonly accepted that you have nodes, connections, and connections are between pins/ports on nodes. 

So if anything, I think using `GraphNodeContainer` as the stem makes more sense from a layman's understanding of the class structure rather than `GraphPortContainer`, but that's just my $0.02.

> The editor crashes when changing Vector Compose `Vector3` to `Vector4` or `Vector2`.

Hmm, this works fine on my end. Could I get some more info about how you're producing this, or the call stack on crash?

> Shouldn't [`GraphFrame`] act like a `Control` when disabled?

I'll look into this, but I believe this down to some hard-coded `Control` behaviour that checks to see if a node's parent is a `Container`, which would be a separate PR to address.

> On drag, snap `position + pivot_offset` to the grid, not just `position`.
> Also, resizing a graph node should resize around the `pivot_offset`, not `position`.

Will do!

> It would be super useful to be able to disable GraphEdit so that nothing is editable and zoom/pan are locked.

Sure! I can add `view_locked` for this purpose. 

> Right now GraphPortContainer and GraphPortContainerIndexed share the same icon.

Yes, and I'd welcome a good icon. I've tried designing a few myself (including one very similar to your description) and had mixed success.

> Is there any reason why all other `Control` children of `GraphEdit` shouldn't act like they are inside a `GraphElement`?

`GraphEdit`'s current behaviour is fairly dependent on properties and methods that `GraphElement` exposes. This opens up a question I think is very useful: what exactly _is_ a `GraphElement`? I believe this UI element is more accurately described as a `ResizeableContainer`, with extra behaviour thrown in to let it be selected, dragged, and themed with a custom minimap panel. This leads to... well, a much broader point.

To be honest, having rewritten this system to this point, I believe there's still one major step towards integrating this system with the engine as a whole and removing the experimental label. This would require yet another major reimplementation, building on top of this PR. Specifically, I believe the following would bring this system much more in line with Godot UI's design up to this point:
- Make `GraphConnection` a node inheriting `Line2D`, and rename it to something more general like `ConnectionLine2D`.
- Rather than inheriting from `GraphElement`, as it is not a `Container`, make `GraphPort` inherit from a new node called `DragHandle`. Additionally, there's an argument to be made here that `GraphPort` should work completely in isolation, no `GraphEdit` required.
- As stated above, `GraphElement` should be refactored into `ResizeableContainer`. This would require selection logic to be extended to work with any `Control`, likely handled by `GraphEdit`, and while the details of this in particular sound _very_ sticky, it would make this system much more powerful.
- Look into making `GraphEdit` inherit from `ViewportContainer`, and perhaps renaming it to something like `GraphView`.

That said, I believe that's not only completely out of scope for this PR, it would be best implemented as _several_ PRs. I think `DragHandle` is something that should be introduced in a dedicated PR, if its existence is warranted (I've implemented this component myself in GDScript a couple times for VNML, so I can vouch for its usefulness). These are potential improvements, best explored in future work.

On the renaming of `GraphNode`, I've similarly felt frustration at the name conflict (everything in Godot is a node already!). I agree that `GraphPortContainer` is more correct, but I don't like how verbose it is, and `GraphPortContainerIndexed` is a hell of a mouthful. Shortenings like `GraphContainer` and `PortContainer` start to become confusing, so we need a separate keyword anyway that better captures the meaning, and node _is_ the correct terminology in this domain. While this _is_ a good time for renaming things, for now, I'd like to leave `GraphNode`/`GraphNodeIndexed` as-is, and revisit them later if better names arise.
